problem: MIPS and Mops/s are used as units but never defined, and the abbreviation 'Mops/s' is not standard (usually MOPS). A second-language reader may not connect MIPS to millions of instructions per second.
fix: At first use write: 'MIPS means million instructions per second, so 200 MIPS = 200,000,000 instructions/s' and use 'MOPS (million operations per second)' instead of 'Mops/s'.

problem: 'The specification is executable: a model produces test data' narrows an executable specification to a test-data generator and can mislead. An executable specification is a simulatable model of the whole system that can be run to check behaviour and to produce expected outputs.
fix: Say: 'The specification is executable: a simulatable model of the system can be run, so both teams take the same test vectors and expected outputs from it.'

problem: The question asks for four stages, but the answer lists six items where 'hardware and software design' can be read as one stage or two, so a student cannot tell how many stages are being counted.
fix: Write the flow as six named stages and say 'any four of: specification, partitioning, interface design, hardware design, software design, co-simulation, integration' or count the list explicitly.

problem: 'Keep auto-exposure control in software because it changes rarely' is misleading: auto-exposure is recomputed every frame. The real reason is that it runs at a low rate (once per frame, about 30 times a second) compared with the per-pixel filter, and needs tuning.
fix: Say: 'Keep auto-exposure in software because it runs only once per frame, needs tuning and may change with the product, while the per-pixel filter runs millions of times per second.'
